# Advanced Verb Tenses

Beyond the basic tenses sit Portuguese's most distinctive forms: the **future subjunctive** (alive in Portuguese, dead in Spanish/French), the **personal infinitive** (no other Romance language has it!), and **compound tenses** with *ter*. Mastering them takes you from intermediate to fluent.

## Core Vocabulary

| Tense | Example | English |
|-------|---------|---------|
| Futuro do indicativo | falarei, falará, falaremos, falarão | I/you/we/they will speak |
| Condicional | falaria, falaríamos, falariam | I/we/they would speak |
| Futuro do subjuntivo | falar, falar, falarmos, falarem | (when/if) I/you/we/they speak |
| Infinitivo pessoal | falar, falares, falar, falarmos, falardes, falarem | for me/you/etc. to speak |
| Pretérito perfeito composto | tenho falado, tens falado | I have been speaking |
| Pretérito mais-que-perfeito | tinha falado, tinha comido | I had spoken / had eaten |

| Trigger for futuro do subj. | Example |
|------------------------------|---------|
| quando | Quando eu chegar, te ligo. |
| se (real future condition) | Se chover, ficaremos em casa. |
| assim que / logo que | Assim que ele chegar, me avise. |
| enquanto | Enquanto você puder, ajude. |

## Example Sentences

- **Quando eu chegar, te ligo.** — When I get there, I'll call you. (futuro do subjuntivo)
- **Se chover amanhã, fico em casa.** — If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
- **Eu te ligaria, mas não tenho seu número.** — I'd call you, but I don't have your number. (conditional)
- **Tenho estudado muito esses dias.** — I've been studying a lot lately. (compound past — ongoing recent)
- **Quando cheguei, ele já tinha saído.** — When I arrived, he had already left. (mais-que-perfeito)
- **É importante para nós sabermos a verdade.** — It's important for us to know the truth. (personal infinitive)
- **Antes de saírem, fechem a porta.** — Before you (pl) leave, close the door. (personal infinitive)

## Grammar / Pronunciation Notes

**Futuro do subjuntivo** — Portuguese is the only major Romance language that still uses this tense. It refers to a future condition that's expected but not yet real. Triggers: *se, quando, assim que, logo que, enquanto, depois que, sempre que*.

How to form it: it looks **identical to the personal infinitive of regular verbs** for the eu/ele forms, with -mos/-em added for plurals. *Se eu falar, se ele falar, se nós falarmos, se eles falarem*. Irregulars: *ser/ir → for; ter → tiver; estar → estiver; fazer → fizer; poder → puder; haver → houver; saber → souber; querer → quiser*.

**Personal infinitive** — Portuguese conjugates the infinitive when its subject is different from the main verb. *É importante para nós sabermos a verdade* — *sabermos* (we to know) makes the implied subject explicit. *Para eu falar, para tu falares, para ele falar, para nós falarmos, para vós falardes, para eles falarem*.

**Compound tenses** with *ter* + past participle:
- *Tenho falado* (perfeito composto): "I have been speaking" (recent ongoing).
- *Tinha falado* (mais-que-perfeito composto): "I had spoken".
- *Terei falado* (futuro composto): "I will have spoken".
- *Teria falado* (condicional composto): "I would have spoken".

The simple **mais-que-perfeito simples** (*falara, comera, partira*) is mostly literary — you'll see it in books, rarely in speech.

## Common Mistakes

- **Don't say** *quando eu chego, te ligo* (in this future-conditional sense) — say *quando eu chegar, te ligo*.
- **Avoid** confusing the personal infinitive with the conjugated form — *para nós saber* is wrong; *para nós sabermos* is right.
- **Don't translate** "I have spoken" as *tenho falado* if you mean a single completed event — that's *eu falei*. *Tenho falado* implies repeated/recent action.
- **Don't use** the simple mais-que-perfeito (*falara*) in speech — say *tinha falado*.

## Try It Yourself

1. Form the futuro do subjuntivo of *fazer*: se eu __, se você __, se nós __, se eles __. (fizer, fizer, fizermos, fizerem)
2. Use personal infinitive: "It's better for us to leave now." → *É melhor nós sairmos agora.*
3. Compound past: "I had already eaten when she called." → *Eu já tinha comido quando ela ligou.*
4. Real conditional: "If you study, you'll pass." → *Se você estudar, você vai passar.*

## Next Steps

You now have the full Portuguese tense system. Move to *Idiomatic Expressions & Proverbs* for the figurative layer, then *CELPE-Bras Exam Preparation* if you want to certify.

# Idiomatic Expressions & Proverbs

Idioms reveal a culture's worldview. Brazilian Portuguese is bursting with vivid, often comic *expressões* and *ditados* — many tied to soccer, food, and animals. Knowing them is the difference between sounding like a textbook and sounding like a Brazilian.

## Core Vocabulary

| Idiom | Literal | Meaning |
|-------|---------|---------|
| chutar o balde | kick the bucket | give up / lose patience |
| pisar na bola | step on the ball | mess up / disappoint someone |
| dar uma mãozinha | give a little hand | lend a hand |
| matar a saudade | kill the longing | reconnect after time apart |
| bater um papo | hit a chat | have a chat |
| pagar mico | pay a monkey | embarrass oneself in public |
| viajar na maionese | travel in the mayonnaise | ramble / talk nonsense |
| descascar um abacaxi | peel a pineapple | deal with a tough problem |
| encher o saco | fill the bag | annoy / bother |
| custar os olhos da cara | cost the eyes of the face | cost a fortune |
| ficar a ver navios | stay watching ships | be left high and dry |
| dar um jeito | give a way | find a workaround (very BR) |
| segurar a vela | hold the candle | be the third wheel |
| meter a mão na massa | put your hand in the dough | get to work |

| Proverb | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **Quem não tem cão, caça com gato.** | If you don't have a dog, hunt with a cat. (Make do.) |
| **Cada macaco no seu galho.** | Each monkey on its branch. (Mind your business.) |
| **De grão em grão, a galinha enche o papo.** | Grain by grain, the hen fills its crop. (Slow and steady.) |
| **Águas passadas não movem moinhos.** | Past waters don't turn mills. (Let bygones be bygones.) |

## Example Sentences

- **Cara, paguei o maior mico ontem na festa!** — Dude, I had the biggest embarrassment yesterday at the party!
- **Vou bater um papo com a galera.** — I'm gonna chat with the gang.
- **Ele tá viajando na maionese, ignora.** — He's talking nonsense, ignore him.
- **Esse carro custou os olhos da cara.** — That car cost a fortune.
- **A gente dá um jeito, não se preocupa.** — We'll find a way, don't worry.
- **Tô descascando um abacaxi no trabalho.** — I'm dealing with a tough problem at work.
- **Não fica enchendo o saco!** — Stop bothering me!

## Grammar / Pronunciation Notes

**Dar um jeito** is so culturally important it has a name: *o jeitinho brasileiro*. It refers to the Brazilian art of finding creative workarounds, often outside formal rules. Hearing *vamos dar um jeito* is reassuring (a solution will appear) — and a window into Brazilian culture.

**Saudade**: famously "untranslatable", but it appears in many idioms: *matar a saudade* (reconnect / catch up), *estou com saudade de você* (I miss you). Saudade is a melancholy longing — for a place, a person, a time.

**Soccer idioms**: Brazil's national sport seeded the language. *Pisar na bola, marcar gol, deu zebra, fazer cera, esticar o jogo* — soccer terms are everywhere, even when nobody's playing.

**Body parts in idioms**: *cara* (face), *boca* (mouth), *mão* (hand), *pé* (foot), *olho* (eye) — body-part idioms are fertile ground for vivid Portuguese: *botar a mão na massa, abrir o olho, dar com a língua nos dentes*.

**Watch the register**: idioms tend to be informal. *Pagar mico* and *encher o saco* are fine with friends but not in business writing.

## Common Mistakes

- **Don't translate** *chutar o balde* as "to die" — in Portuguese, it means "to give up", not the English idiom for dying.
- **Avoid** literal translation of *quem não tem cão* — it's a saying about resourcefulness, not animals.
- **Don't say** *encher o saco* in formal contexts — it's mildly vulgar.
- **Don't overdo** idioms — one or two per conversation is natural; six in a row sounds like a foreigner who memorized a list.

## Try It Yourself

1. Use one idiom in a sentence about your day: *Hoje preciso meter a mão na massa.*
2. Match: "lend a hand" → *dar uma mãozinha*; "rip-off price" → *custou os olhos da cara*.
3. Pick a proverb and explain its meaning in Portuguese to yourself.
4. Listen for one idiom in a Brazilian YouTube video — write it down.

## Next Steps

Native sounding now. Move to *CELPE-Bras Exam Preparation* if you want a credential, or revisit *Brazilian Media & Literature* with new ears for these idioms.

# CELPE-Bras Exam Preparation

The **CELPE-Bras** is Brazil's official Portuguese certification, recognized worldwide for university admission, professional licensing, and immigration. It tests communicative competence — not grammar drills — across four skills, and grades you on a single scale: Intermediário, Intermediário Superior, Avançado, Avançado Superior.

## Core Vocabulary

| CELPE-Bras concept | English |
|--------------------|---------|
| CELPE-Bras | Certificado de Proficiência em Língua Portuguesa para Estrangeiros |
| nível | level |
| compreensão (oral / escrita) | (oral / written) comprehension |
| produção (oral / escrita) | (oral / written) production |
| parte coletiva | collective part (listening/reading + writing tasks) |
| parte individual | individual part (oral interview ~20 min) |
| tarefa | task |
| elemento provocador | prompt material (video, audio, text) |
| interlocutor | interviewer |
| avaliador | grader |
| inscrição | registration |
| edital | exam announcement / regulations |
| certificado | certificate |
| nota | grade |

## Example Sentences

- **Vou prestar a CELPE-Bras em outubro.** — I'm taking the CELPE-Bras in October.
- **Cada tarefa parte de um elemento provocador.** — Each task starts from a prompt material.
- **A parte individual é uma entrevista de cerca de 20 minutos.** — The individual part is an interview of about 20 minutes.
- **Quero tirar o nível Avançado para entrar na universidade.** — I want to score Advanced to enter university.
- **Me inscrevi pelo site do Inep.** — I registered through Inep's website.
- **Estudei com simulados durante três meses.** — I studied with mock exams for three months.

## Grammar / Pronunciation Notes

**Exam structure** (current format):
- **Parte Coletiva (~3h)**: 4 written tasks. Each starts with an *elemento provocador* (a video, audio, or text). You read/listen, then produce a piece of writing in a specific genre — letter, article, email, etc. Genre-awareness is critical.
- **Parte Individual (~20 min)**: face-to-face oral interview. Three brief stimuli (image cards) prompt conversation about everyday topics, then more abstract themes.

**Grading scale**: a single grade from 0 to 5 places you in Intermediário, Intermediário Superior, Avançado, or Avançado Superior. Below threshold = no certificate. Most universities accept Intermediário Superior or higher.

**Genre-awareness is everything**: a CELPE writing task isn't a "write 200 words on X". It's "write a letter to the editor", or "write an email to a friend", or "write an op-ed". Match register, structure, and conventions of the genre.

**Common task genres to practice**: carta do leitor, e-mail formal/informal, artigo de opinião, reportagem, relato pessoal, post de blog. Each has its own opening, closing, and tone.

**Speaking tips**: speak fluently, even with errors. The grader scores communicative effectiveness, not perfection. Don't whisper; don't switch to English. Use linkers (*além disso, por outro lado, em primeiro lugar*) to sound organized.

## Common Mistakes

- **Don't ignore** the elemento provocador — your written task must clearly engage with it.
- **Avoid** writing a generic essay when the task asks for a letter or email — wrong genre = lower score.
- **Don't mix** registers — a formal letter shouldn't suddenly say *cara*, *valeu*, *kkkk*.
- **Don't memorize** rigid templates — graders spot generic openings and discount them.

## Try It Yourself

1. Find a past CELPE-Bras prompt (Inep publishes them) and write a 200-word response in the requested genre.
2. Practice the oral: pick an image, talk about it for 1 minute, then explain a related abstract idea for 2 minutes.
3. Time yourself: 3 hours for the collective part — full simulation.
4. Find a study partner or tutor for at least 10 oral practice sessions before the real exam.

## Next Steps

If you've reached this point, you're ready for the exam. Practice past prompts, get oral feedback, and continue immersion through Brazilian media. Boa sorte na prova!
